newsitem.title: PERU: Shots heard at Peru hostage siege site - radio.
newsitem.headline: Shots heard at Peru hostage siege site - radio.

text.p: Several shots were heard early on Tuesday morning at the site of the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima where Marxist rebels hold 72 hostages, local radio reported.
The Radio Programas del Peru (RPP) radio station said at least five shots were heard at about 5:00 a.m. (1000 GMT) coming from the residence.
The shots were immediately followed by silence and there was no movement inside of the diplomatic compound, witnesses said.

Reuters photographers stationed about a block from the building said they heard several shots. The residence was seized by about 15 heavily armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels Dec. 17.
Police on guard around the building did not appear to be alarmed by the shots, witnesses said. "They (the rebels) are just trying to grab our attention," one police officer told Reuters at the site.

The rebels have fired what police have described as warning shots into the air several times during the 49-day siege. The shooting was apparently the first at the site since the guerrillas fired at police aboard a convoy in front of the residence on Jan. 27.
